title: An episode is closed by evidence, or not at all
intro: A provider that is killed sends no end event, and the episode it opened stays open for ever. Recovery closes it — but only when the evidence says its client is gone, and never by guessing. Every subject has a --check that writes nothing, and the measurement that decided each verdict is printed before anything is done with it.

scenarios.title: The plan, and the measurement behind it

stdout_contains: live: this process is inside it

scenarios.explain: Every candidate's last sign of life is printed, including the ones nothing will happen to, so a wrong predicate is visible in the output rather than in its consequences. The dry run writes nothing at all.

scenarios.title: Closing the one whose client is gone
scenarios.explain: The record carries what the open record and the episode's own ledger lines prove. Its commits and changed_files are the explicit empty list and it states no head: the working tree at recovery time belongs to whoever is working now, and stamping it onto an episode that stopped days ago would be a record that looks exactly like a true one.

scenarios.title: With nothing degraded
scenarios.explain: Absence is an answer. A clean store exits 0 and says so, rather than treating having nothing to do as a failure.

scenarios.title: A subject this command does not have
scenarios.explain: A misspelled subject is refused rather than folded into the default. A recovery command that silently did something other than what was asked is the one that must not exist.
